request.description: Train a fresh PPO candidate with the currently recorded baseline recipe for the full 120,000-step startup allocation.
request.rationale: The decisive initial distinction is whether a learned torque policy under the existing implementation can acquire and sustain the required uninterrupted hold, versus whether its apparent limitations concentrate in the official inner-radius region omitted from baseline exposure. There is no candidate or behavior evidence yet. This training run creates the first reproducible artifact and a learning trajectory; after completion, training proxies will nominate (not establish) which saved checkpoint to evaluate on the official development distribution with reach/hold and target-stratified diagnostics. The recipe's 14–20 cm training range is a known limitation, so this run is a baseline capability probe, not evidence that the coverage gap causes any later failure. A checkpoint with broadly successful reach and hold would reduce the urgency of altering control; failures after timely reach with interrupted/short holds would prioritize stabilization, while failures concentrated at 6–14 cm would motivate a controlled coverage investigation. The result is worthwhile now because no prior artifact exists to measure or compare.

request.description: Compare the first late-plateau checkpoint with the terminal checkpoint on the fixed task-reference panel and a paired 200-episode official-range research panel, retaining episode diagnostics.
request.rationale: T1's training proxy reaches 0.97 at 110,592 steps and remains 0.96–0.97 through 120,832, but those proxies are generated under the baseline 14–20 cm training sampler and cannot establish official-distribution success. The two checkpoints are complete artifacts from the same fresh run and both are supported by the observed plateau; comparing them on the same development evidence tests whether the additional training after the first plateau improves the actual task rather than assuming the terminal artifact is best. The protected task-reference panel assesses saved-policy performance under the protected development execution path. The paired research panel uses official target sampling and preserves per-episode first-reach, maximum hold, interruptions, radius and angle so that failures can be separated into reach/hold and target-region patterns. If the later checkpoint materially improves protected success without changing the relevant failure profile, it is the stronger candidate artifact; similar results imply no demonstrated benefit from the additional training. Timely reach followed by interrupted/short holds would prioritize stabilization; failures concentrated at 6–14 cm would motivate a controlled coverage test, but this comparison cannot establish coverage as the cause because training exposure and all other recipe factors are common to both checkpoints. Disagreement between protected and research outcomes would limit mechanism claims and call for investigating execution-semantics differences. These outcomes discriminate whether to continue this baseline recipe, investigate hold control, or test official-range coverage, directly toward the 98% complete-episode goal.

request.reason: Among the only two candidates measured, T1:checkpoint-110592 has the stronger completed-episode evidence: 90.5% (181/200) on the fixed task-reference panel versus 85.5% (171/200) for T1:checkpoint-120832, and 86% versus 84% on the paired official-range research panel. The paired research outcomes are modest (four discordant episodes, all won by this candidate), so this is a provisional best-known role, not proof of broad superiority or achievement of the 98% goal. It is the more defensible artifact for continuity while a causal training-exposure comparison is investigated.

request.candidates_and_roles: Best-known: T1:checkpoint-110592, explicitly assigned by E1 based on M1 (90.5% task-reference; 86% paired research) versus T1:checkpoint-120832 (85.5%; 84%). No working candidate. T1:checkpoint-120832 is an available measured comparison artifact, not the selected best-known. Neither is near the 98% objective or officially assessed. request.current_goal_gap: T1's baseline PPO training proxy reached 0.97 success on its 14–20 cm training range, but this does not transfer to official performance. On the protected task-reference panel the better measured checkpoint, T1:checkpoint-110592, succeeded on 181/200 episodes (90.5%); on a separate paired official-range research panel it succeeded on 172/200 (86%). This is 15 fewer successes than the 196/200 final-panel threshold on the task-reference panel and 24 failures in the research panel. No final official assessment has occurred.
request.current_synthesis: Observed: No candidate or previous operation existed at startup. T1 was a fresh PPO run under unchanged baseline sources, seed 42, 120,000 requested steps; it completed 120,832 steps after rollout rounding and archived 24 checkpoints. The training success proxy rose from 0 to 0.97 by 110,592 steps and remained 0.96–0.97 through 120,832 on the baseline 14–20 cm sampler. The run therefore establishes an executable baseline recipe and a plateau, not development success under the official distribution. M1 compared the first plateau checkpoint (110,592) with the terminal checkpoint (120,832), both from the same run and recipe. T1:checkpoint-110592 scored 90.5% (181/200) on the fixed task-reference panel and 86% (172/200) on the paired 200-episode official-range research panel. T1:checkpoint-120832 scored 85.5% (171/200) and 84% (168/200), respectively. On the paired research panel there were four discordant episodes, all won by checkpoint-110592; this is a modest artifact-level advantage, not strong evidence of a generally superior method or of a cause. The two panel types used different seeds, so their score differences do not isolate evaluator semantics. The later checkpoint had no measured task advantage despite similar training proxies; it is not privileged because it is terminal. The task-reference failure rows for both checkpoints are overwhelmingly at radii below about 11.5 cm, with a few failures at larger radii. In the research diagnostics, checkpoint-110592 had 28 failures: 21 never entered tolerance at a sampled control step, all on targets at 6.1–11.4 cm; seven reached tolerance but never completed a 100-step uninterrupted hold. Checkpoint-120832 had 32 failures: 23 never entered tolerance, also all at 6.1–11.4 cm, and nine reached tolerance but did not complete the hold. Many other inner-radius targets succeeded, and the no-reach episodes cluster in particular target-angle sectors; thus radial training coverage is a consequential hypothesis, not an established cause. Successful/reaching episodes typically first entered tolerance within roughly 5–20 control steps, so the reset singularity is real but the current evidence does not identify slow escape as the dominant failure for reached targets. The observations preserve only control-step diagnostics, not joint/torque trajectories or within-step excursions. Interpretations: The source model's kinematic feasibility conclusion remains unrevised; measured failures concern policy behavior, not proof of geometric impossibility. The training sampler omits 6–14 cm, which is 4/7 (about 57%) of official radial probability under the uniform-radius sampler and requires more folded configurations. Concentrated inner-radius failures support prioritizing a controlled coverage test. Their angular concentration, repeated no-reach patterns across the paired checkpoints, and several hold failures leave plausible alternatives: target-sector/IK-branch selection, difficulty leaving the singular reset for those configurations, and stabilization after first reach. The comparison changed checkpoint time within one training trajectory, not training distribution, and cannot establish any of those mechanisms. Dynamic path costs, compiled inertias/contact response, and within-control-step hold semantics remain unmeasured; they should change the immediate direction only if coverage-focused work fails or later traces implicate them. A research-evaluation success is measured at the accessible control-step cadence; it does not resolve hidden substep checks or certify the official final panel.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved distinction is whether the main actionable development gap comes from the known radial exposure mismatch (especially 6–11.5 cm targets) or instead from angle/IK-branch-dependent acquisition from the singular reset and/or hold stabilization. M1's repeated no-reach failures below about 11.5 cm support the exposure hypothesis, but inner-radius successes, angular clustering, and post-reach hold failures prevent causal attribution. A useful discriminator is a fresh full-budget run holding PPO architecture, parameters, source except the training-radius lower bound, seed and evaluation protocol fixed, changing exposure from 14–20 cm to the official 6–20 cm; measure both candidates on the same held-out task-reference and research panels and inspect success, first reach, maximum hold, interruptions and target radius/angle. Improvement concentrated among inner-radius targets would support coverage as a contributor; no improvement or persistent angle-specific no-reach failures would redirect toward reset/branch/trajectory mechanisms; timely reaches followed by interrupted holds would prioritize stabilization. Because this is one recipe and one seed, either result is limited to that implementation and would not prove or disprove broader coverage methods. If coverage does not change the decision, branch-conditioned joint/endpoint trajectories and torque response are the next physical discriminator; compiled dynamics and within-step hold details remain open but are not required to prioritize the first comparison.
request.human_goal_connection: The sole objective is at least 98% complete-episode success under the official 6–20 cm, full-angle target distribution, where success requires the uninterrupted 100-step/2-second hold. This startup work established a first learned baseline, measured two plausible checkpoints on development evidence, and chose an evidence-backed best-known artifact; both measured artifacts remain materially below the goal.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Startup evidence is sufficient to checkpoint and enter goal review, not to request official assessment. The proposed next direction is a bounded, seed-matched test of the official-radius training-coverage hypothesis, subject to goal review's independent choice. The prospective comparison changes only the training-radius lower bound and evaluates complete episodes plus target-stratified reach/hold diagnostics; if it improves inner-radius success, coverage becomes a supported contributor worth developing, while persistent angular/branch or hold failures redirect the next bounded work. A null/limited result would be unresolved for the broader method, not proof that coverage cannot help. Do not infer causation from M1's checkpoint comparison.
request.next_question: Does changing only the baseline training-radius range from 14–20 cm to the official 6–20 cm improve complete-episode success, particularly for inner-radius targets, or do the observed angle-specific no-reach and post-reach hold failures persist and make reset/IK-branch control or stabilization the more consequential next direction?

Evaluate it on the same fixed task-reference panel and the same 200-episode research panel used for T1:checkpoint-110592, with paired outcomes and target-stratified success, first-reach step, maximum held steps and hold interruptions. Close with the measured candidate comparison and the behavioral pattern: inner-radius gains support coverage as a contributor; little/no gain with persistent angle-specific no-reach failures redirects toward reset/branch acquisition; timely reaches followed by failed holds redirects toward stabilization. One seed supports only this recipe-specific conclusion; a null result does not disprove broader coverage methods.

Baseline training excludes 6–14 cm, about 57% of official uniform-radius probability; in M1, 21/28 and 23/32 research-panel failures never reached tolerance, all at 6.1–11.4 cm, while 7 and 9 other failures did reach but did not complete the hold. Testing whether coverage changes complete-episode outcomes therefore directly addresses the current goal gap while preserving competing acquisition and stabilization explanations.

request.rationale: Official assessment is terminal and the strongest measured candidate is materially below goal on both development panels, so its expected chance of meeting 196/200 is not compelling enough to spend the only assessment now. Further training on the unchanged recipe is also weakly supported: T1's success proxy rose to 0.94–0.96 by about 80k, fluctuated at 0.94–0.97 thereafter, and M1 found the terminal checkpoint 10/200 below the earlier plateau checkpoint on task-reference and 4/200 worse on the paired research panel. The proposed experiment is a genuinely untested training exposure, not a relabeling of T1: the inspected training environment has a single 14–20 cm sampler constant, T1 used the unchanged source commit and baseline PPO settings, and the requested comparison changes that range to 6–20 cm while holding seed and remaining recipe fixed. Its full training cost is substantial, but the known 57% radial omission and repeated inner-radius no-reach failures make it more likely to improve the route to the goal than another baseline checkpoint measurement. M1 also supplies counterevidence: many inner-radius targets succeeded, failures clustered by angle, and 7–9 failures per candidate were post-reach hold failures, so coverage is a hypothesis rather than an established cause. Research diagnostics sample control steps and cannot establish hidden within-step hold behavior or certify the official panel; this experiment can direct development but cannot substitute for final assessment.

request.current_synthesis:
Observed: T1 was a fresh 120,000-requested-step PPO run (120,832 actual after rollout rounding), seed 42, under unchanged source commit 95e92976dddec5715a678cde36263ee0b19dcf8e and baseline parameters. The preserved training trajectory rose from zero success proxy through 40,960 steps, reached 0.96 around 79,872, then fluctuated mostly 0.94–0.97 through 120,832; 110,592 was the first archived late-plateau checkpoint and the terminal proxy was not better. This proxy came from the 14–20 cm training sampler, not the official distribution. M1 measured two checkpoints from this same run: T1:checkpoint-110592 scored 181/200 (90.5%) task-reference and 172/200 (86%) on the research panel; T1:checkpoint-120832 scored 171/200 (85.5%) and 168/200 (84%). The panels use different seeds/semantics and their aggregate rates should not be interpreted as a direct evaluator comparison. On the paired research panel, the four discordant episodes all favored checkpoint-110592; this is a modest difference between these artifacts, not a general training-time effect or mechanism. In M1's research diagnostics, checkpoint-110592 had 28 failures: 21 never sampled within tolerance and all 21 targets were 6.1–11.4 cm; seven reached but did not complete the uninterrupted 100-step hold. Checkpoint-120832 had 32 failures: 23 no-reach cases, all 6.1–11.4 cm, and nine post-reach hold failures. Many other inner-radius episodes succeeded; no-reach cases also cluster in some angular sectors (mostly negative-angle sectors in the inspected rows, with exceptions), so radius alone does not explain failure. Several successful/reaching episodes reached within roughly 5–20 control steps, which weighs against universal slow escape from reset as the dominant cause but does not rule out angle-conditioned acquisition difficulty. Diagnostics are sampled at control steps and contain no joint, torque, or within-step traces. Task-reference failure rows are also predominantly at inner radii, with some larger-radius failures, but that fixed panel is not the same seed panel as the research diagnostics.

Interpretation updated against pi_workspace/scientific_model.md: Its kinematic consequence remains unrevised: both elbow-sign IK branches are joint-limit feasible throughout the official region, so these behavioral failures do not establish geometric impossibility. This keeps the decision on learned acquisition/trajectory/hold, not workspace expansion; branch-specific residuals, limit margins, and trajectories would revise that view if they contradicted the calculated feasible solutions. The fully extended reset is rank deficient and every target begins outside tolerance, so leaving the reset can matter; however, early observed reaches mean the present evidence does not justify making generic singularity escape the lead explanation. If inner no-reach cases remain after broader training coverage, target-conditioned joint/end-point traces and branch errors from reset would redirect work toward reset/IK-branch control. The direct bounded motor commands are held across ten physics substeps and there is no authored position servo: reaching is not holding. M1's seven and nine post-reach failures make stabilization a real competing limitation; if the new candidate reaches inner targets but still loses the hold, full error/velocity/command traces through hold and maximum-hold/interruptions would support a stabilization direction. The model's compiled inertia/contact response remains unknown and could change approach/braking conclusions, but neither panel identifies it; posture-conditioned torque response, inertias and contact counts would matter if traces show path- or posture-specific dynamic failures. The observation omits hold progress and episode time, which could make task state partially observed, but no current result attributes failure to that omission; matched physical states with different hold histories/horizons and saved-runtime decisions would be needed before changing the observation or policy memory. Protected within-control-step occupancy is also unresolved: the public diagnostics sample after a control interval and cannot establish substep excursions. The official 100-step contract remains authoritative; protected trajectory evidence or the final assessment would revise claims about actual official behavior, and no development panel certifies it.

The baseline training environment has a single 14–20 cm sampler constant, while the official uniform-radius range is 6–20 cm; thus 8/14 (4/7, about 57%) of official radial probability is omitted and more-folded postures are required. This is evidence for a consequential coverage test, not proof of cause: inner-radius successes, angle clustering, and post-reach failures are counterevidence to a radius-only account. The proposed 6–20 cm run would retain the PPO architecture, parameters, reward, observation, runtime, task mechanics, seed and budget, changing only training exposure. Improvement concentrated among inner-radius complete-episode outcomes would support coverage as a contributor in this recipe; unchanged angle-conditioned no-reach would redirect toward acquisition/branch control; successful reaching with interrupted holds would direct work toward stabilization. One fresh seed cannot establish a general result about all coverage methods, and a null result would not disprove that broader method. There is no completed result from I1 yet.
request.decision_frontier: The campaign must choose between a terminal assessment of a candidate with 90.5% task-reference and 86% research-panel performance, or bounded work with a credible prospect of changing the candidate before that assessment. The immediate scientific distinction is whether exposing PPO to the missing official inner radii materially improves complete-episode success, or whether the repeated angle-conditioned no-reach and post-reach hold failures remain. I1 will compare a fresh full-budget, seed-42 run changing only the sampler lower bound (14 to 6 cm) against T1:checkpoint-110592 on the same fixed task-reference panel and the same paired research episode seeds, using success and radius/angle-stratified first reach, maximum hold and interruptions. Inner-radius gains would support further coverage development; no meaningful gain with persistent angular no-reach would favor reset/branch/trajectory evidence; reaching without uninterrupted holds would prioritize stabilization. This is recipe- and seed-specific. Compiled dynamics/contact, omitted hold/time state, and protected substep semantics remain uncertainties with specified discriminators above, but current aggregate and control-step evidence does not make them more decision-relevant than the sampler comparison. If the planned training or measurement fails or lacks those diagnostics, the distinction remains unresolved rather than counting as a negative scientific result.

request.description: Train a fresh baseline PPO candidate for the full 120,000-step allocation with the training target-radius sampler changed from 14–20 cm to 6–20 cm; all other baseline recipe components remain unchanged.
request.rationale: I1 tests whether the baseline policy’s observed inner-radius failures are helped by exposing training to the missing 6–14 cm region, versus angle-conditioned acquisition or post-reach stabilization remaining limiting. Source inspection showed T1 used the unchanged 14–20 cm sampler; the reviewed one-line source change changes only its lower bound to 6 cm, while preserving the PPO parameters, reward, observations, task mechanics, runtime and seed. Run the full seed-42 allocation to generate the changed-exposure learning trajectory and checkpoints. The proxy trajectory will nominate a development-measured checkpoint in this new exposure context but cannot establish official-distribution success. Subsequent paired task-reference and 200-episode research evaluation against T1:checkpoint-110592, with target-stratified success, first reach, maximum hold and interruptions, can show whether gains concentrate at inner radii, whether angular no-reach persists, or whether reaches are still followed by failed holds. A positive pattern would support coverage as a contributor in this specific recipe; unchanged failure patterns would redirect toward acquisition/branch or stabilization evidence, not disprove broader coverage methods.

request.description: Compare the selected 6–20 cm exposure candidate T2:checkpoint-120832 with the best-known baseline T1:checkpoint-110592 on the fixed task-reference panel and the same paired 200-episode official-range research panel, retaining target-stratified reach and hold diagnostics.
request.rationale: T2 is the one-factor coverage implementation in I1: the reviewed change altered only the training radius lower bound (14 to 6 cm), with fresh seed 42 and the baseline PPO parameters; recorded provenance identifies robot_learning/training/environment.py as the changed source. Its success proxy reached a run-high 0.53 at 120,832 steps and had climbed monotonically over the late trajectory, while ep_rew_mean peaked earlier and declined. Select this checkpoint for its highest observed goal-aligned training-success proxy, not merely because it is terminal; the proxy is training-context evidence, not development performance. Measure the candidate on the protected fixed task-reference panel and on the exact 200-seed research panel used for T1:checkpoint-110592. Re-run the reference artifact on the research panel in this operation so the paired comparison is computed under the same evaluator and episode seeds. The research artifact records complete-episode success, target radius and angle, first-reach step, maximum held steps and hold interruptions. If the changed-exposure candidate improves complete success especially on inner radii and reduces inner no-reach failures while completing holds, that supports coverage as a contributor in this recipe and could motivate further development of this exposure. If it does not improve, or failures remain angle-specific no-reach despite exposure, prioritize reset/IK-branch acquisition evidence; if it reaches but loses uninterrupted holds, prioritize stabilization. A lower result is still only a one-run, one-seed artifact comparison and does not disprove broader coverage methods. Neither development panel certifies the official 196/200 threshold.

request.description: Analyze the complete M2 paired research panel for radius- and angle-stratified success, first reach and hold behavior, validating episode-seed and target alignment.
request.rationale: M2 establishes an artifact-level disadvantage for the changed-exposure candidate (153/200 versus 172/200 research success; 21 reference wins, 2 candidate wins) but its aggregate comparison does not show whether the difference comes from radius-conditioned acquisition, angular no-reach, or post-reach hold failure. The PI-owned analyzer validates all 200 episode outcomes against diagnostics, joins by episode seed, checks identical target coordinates between the candidates, and reports paired wins plus success, no-reach/post-reach failures, first-reach timing, max held steps and interruptions by official-radius bins and 45-degree sectors. This directly satisfies I1's target-stratified discriminator and can determine whether the single tested 6–20 cm recipe merits further coverage work or whether the next direction should shift toward acquisition/branch behavior or stabilization. The analysis is limited to recorded control-step research diagnostics; it cannot establish protected within-step occupancy or official benchmark success.

request.outcome: I1's required recipe-specific comparison is complete. T2 was a fresh 120,000-requested-step seed-42 PPO run (120,832 actual), with a reviewed source change limited to the training-radius lower bound from 14 cm to 6 cm; the remaining baseline PPO parameters and task/evaluation code were unchanged. The selected checkpoint T2:checkpoint-120832 had the highest T2 training-success proxy (0.53, still rising late; reward peaked earlier at 110,592), so it was selected by its changed-exposure learning trajectory rather than terminal status alone. M2 measured it at 151/200 task-reference successes (75.5%) and 153/200 research-panel successes (76.5%), versus T1:checkpoint-110592's 181/200 task-reference and 172/200 on the same paired research seeds. The paired research result had 2 T2 wins, 21 T1 wins and 177 ties. M3's validated target-stratified analysis found only a narrow +1 success for T2 in 6–<10 cm (36/57 versus 35/57), but 10–<14 cm fell by 7 successes (44/53 versus 51/53); across 6–14 cm T2 had 80/110 versus T1's 86/110. T2 also fell in 14–<18 cm (50/66 versus 62/66) and 18–20 cm (23/24 versus 24/24). T2's 47 research failures comprised 45 no-reach and 2 post-reach failures, compared with T1's 21 no-reach and 7 post-reach failures. T2's no-reach failures were strongly angle-conditioned: 31/32 failures in [-180,-135) degrees and 8/16 in [135,180) were no-reach, with large paired deficits in those sectors. The measured T2 artifact therefore does not support improved complete-episode success from this one 6–20 cm recipe and seed; the behavioral evidence shifts the next development priority toward target-angle-conditioned acquisition/reset/IK-branch trajectories rather than further coverage tuning or stabilization as the dominant current failure. This does not prove the radius change caused the artifact-level difference, disprove other coverage methods, or certify the official benchmark.
request.reason: The inquiry's closure condition required one fresh full-budget, seed-42 run changing only the training lower radius; trajectory-informed selection of a checkpoint from that changed exposure context; evaluation on the same fixed task-reference panel and paired 200-seed research panel used for T1:checkpoint-110592; and target-stratified complete success, reach, max-hold and interruption evidence. T2, M2 and M3 satisfy those conditions. The comparative result is materially negative for the selected T2 artifact, with only a +1 success in the smallest radial bin, a net -19/200 paired research outcomes overall, and substantial angle-conditioned no-reach failures. That is sufficient to redirect the bounded inquiry to acquisition/branch evidence while preserving the one-seed and control-step diagnostic limits. The 98% human goal remains unmet, and only the 86% development-best candidate T1:checkpoint-110592 remains best-known; no official assessment has occurred.

request.current_synthesis:
Observed: T2 was a fresh seed-42 baseline PPO run with 120,000 requested and 120,832 actual steps. The reviewed source change altered only TRAINING_TARGET_RADIUS_RANGE in robot_learning/training/environment.py, from (0.14, 0.20) to (0.06, 0.20); PPO settings, reward, observations, task mechanics, evaluation and saved runtime were unchanged. T2's training-success proxy rose throughout the later trajectory from 0.36 at 110,592 to 0.49 at 115,712 and 0.53 at 120,832, while ep_rew_mean peaked earlier at 110,592 and declined. T2:checkpoint-120832 was therefore selected because it had the highest observed success proxy in the changed exposure context, not because it was terminal. Its proxy is not comparable to T1's 0.97 under the baseline 14–20 cm training sampler. The other T2 checkpoints remain unmeasured; 110,592 had the reward peak but a 0.36 success proxy, and 115,712 had a 0.49 proxy. They are not presumed to perform like the measured terminal checkpoint, but the observed success trajectory gave no stronger nominee than 120,832.

M2 measured T2:checkpoint-120832 at 151/200 (75.5%) task-reference and 153/200 (76.5%) on the same 200-seed research panel as T1:checkpoint-110592. The repeated T1 research measurement scored 172/200; paired comparison was 2 T2 wins, 21 T1 wins and 177 ties. T1's fixed task-reference result from M1 was 181/200 (90.5%). Do not compare task-reference and research rates as if they were one evaluator. M3 joined the complete M2 research outcomes and diagnostics by episode seed, verified identical targets and the 100-step success/hold consistency, and returned radius/angle strata. At 6–<10 cm T2 had 36/57 successes versus T1's 35/57 (paired wins 2 to 1); at 10–<14 it had 44/53 versus 51/53 (0 to 7 paired wins); at 14–<18 it had 50/66 versus 62/66 (0 to 12); at 18–20 it had 23/24 versus 24/24 (0 to 1). Combined 6–14 cm outcomes were 80/110 for T2 versus 86/110 for T1. Thus the only gain is one episode in the smallest radial bin, not a broad inner-radius improvement. T2's failure count is principally acquisition: 45 failures lacked a sampled first reach versus 21 for T1; only 2 T2 failures were post-reach versus 7 for T1. T2's no-reach pattern is strongly angular: 31/32 targets in [-180,-135) degrees and 8/16 in [135,180) were no-reach failures. In those sectors T2 succeeded on 1/32 and 8/16, versus T1's 14/32 and 15/16. Among episodes that did reach, first reaches were generally early (mean 12.71 control steps T2 versus 11.86 T1); this does not imply universal failure to escape reset, but target-sector acquisition is a stronger current distinction than hold stabilization.

Interpretation against pi_workspace/scientific_model.md: Both elbow-sign IK branches remain calculated as joint-limit feasible throughout the official region; observed failures still do not establish geometric impossibility or justify changing workspace. The fully extended reset remains rank-deficient and all targets begin outside tolerance. Early reaches, together with the sharply angle-conditioned no-reach sectors, argue against treating generic slow singularity escape as established; they make branch/trajectory acquisition from reset the next consequential mechanism to test. Target-conditioned joint/end-point trajectories, IK-branch errors and limit margins from reset could support or revise that direction. The specific 6–20 cm exposure implementation did not improve the selected candidate and its deficit is broad, with particularly severe angular acquisition failures. This is a one-run, one-seed artifact comparison, not proof that the lower radius caused the deficit and not evidence against broader coverage methods. The direct bounded motor commands are still held across ten physics substeps without an authored position servo, so reach and sustained hold remain distinct. T1 had seven post-reach failures and T2 two, meaning stabilization is not disproved, but it does not explain the T2 candidate's larger failure burden; full error/velocity/command traces through hold would change priority if a stronger-acquisition artifact still loses holds. Compiled inertia/contact response remains unknown and could affect posture-specific trajectories or braking; it becomes decision-relevant if joint/torque traces show path-specific dynamic limits. Omitted hold progress and episode clock have no evidence tying them to the current no-reach pattern; matched physical states with different hold histories/horizons would be needed before changing observation or policy memory. Research diagnostics remain sampled at control steps and cannot establish protected within-step occupancy. The official uninterrupted 100-step criterion remains authoritative; protected substep traces or the official assessment could revise claims about implementation-specific behavior, and no development panel certifies official success.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved next distinction is whether T1's remaining angle-conditioned no-reach failures reflect branch selection or trajectory acquisition from the singular reset, versus another policy/dynamic path limitation; the current diagnostics have no joint, torque or within-step trajectories. Evidence that would change the next development direction is target-angle/radius-conditioned q, qdot and endpoint-error trajectories from reset through first reach, branch-specific IK errors and joint-limit margins, paired with eventual reach/hold outcomes. A consistent branch-specific failure or reset exit problem would support redesign/testing of branch-aware acquisition; early, accurate reaches followed by velocity/error drift or interrupted holds would instead elevate stabilization and call for command/torque/error traces through the entire hold. Compiled inertia/contact response could alter these path interpretations if those traces show posture-specific dynamics; it is not yet the leading distinction. The T2 coverage comparison closes I1 with a negative result for its measured artifact, not a general rejection of coverage. At goal review, compare the still-underperforming best-known T1 candidate's prospects for terminal official assessment against the value and cost of this acquisition-focused discriminator; inquiry closure itself commits to neither.

The strongest candidate is materially below the goal on distinct development panels (T1:checkpoint-110592 scored 181/200 task-reference and 172/200 research), and the official panel is fixed and ends the campaign; the completed development evidence gives little reason to expect 196/200 from this artifact. M4 measured the plausible untested T1:checkpoint-115712, nominated by its 0.97 training-success proxy and slightly higher reward, at 179/200 task-reference and the same 172/200 research successes as T1:checkpoint-110592, with only 2 wins, 2 losses and 196 ties; it supplies no stronger artifact. M3 provides a consequential discriminator but not its mechanism: for T1, 21 failures had no sampled first reach and 7 occurred after reach; 14 no-reach and 4 post-reach failures were in [-180,-135) degrees. Even the hypothetical correction of all 21 no-reach outcomes with the 7 post-reach failures unchanged would produce only 193/200 on that research panel, so the inherited acquisition-versus-stabilization framing is too exclusive: both categories may need attention to reach 196. The initial model's two joint-limit-feasible IK branches and rank-deficient fully extended reset make branch/trajectory acquisition plausible, but do not prove it; early first reaches among reached episodes counter a generic slow-escape claim. Direct bounded torque commands without an authored position servo make braking and uninterrupted hold plausible contributors, while M3's seven post-reach failures support retaining that alternative. The proposed trajectory instrument differs from prior work: M3 stratified sampled reach/hold outcomes by target, but recorded no joint, branch-error, command or torque trajectories, and T2 tested a changed training-radius sampler rather than an acquisition or stabilization intervention. If trajectories show branch/reset-exit errors associated with no-reach episodes, acquisition redesign becomes credible; if acquisition looks comparable but post-reach velocity/error or commands drift, stabilization deserves explicit work; if both patterns occur, both are required; if they do not distinguish these alternatives, this inquiry will not justify a mechanism-specific redesign. Current research samples cannot resolve excursions between control steps or certify the protected evaluator, so only official assessment can establish the final goal.

Importantly, the inherited framing of acquisition redesign versus stabilization as a binary choice was too exclusive: if all 21 no-reach failures were corrected on this panel while all 7 post-reach failures remained, the result would be only 193/200, below the 196 target. Both failure classes remain consequential if this panel reflects the goal distribution.

T2 was a fresh seed-42 run changing only the training sampler minimum from 14 to 6 cm. Interpretation against the initial physical model: Both elbow-sign IK branches are calculated joint-limit-feasible across the official workspace; target geometry alone is not an established cause. Direct bounded torque commands are held across ten physics substeps without an authored position servo, so braking and hold stabilization remain distinct from first reach; M3's seven post-reach failures make them decision-relevant. Joint/command/torque/error traces through the whole hold could elevate stabilization; path-dependent accelerations or braking in such traces would make compiled inertial/contact response consequential. Existing research diagnostics are sampled at control steps and do not establish protected within-step occupancy. M4 and M3 support a mechanism inquiry rather than immediate assessment: the best evidence-backed candidate is substantially below target, the plausible unmeasured late checkpoint is not stronger, and official assessment is terminal. The proposed inquiry is not another coverage trial: M3 compared target-stratified sampled outcomes but supplied no reset-to-reach joint, IK-branch, command or torque trajectories and no full hold traces.
